content:
iPhone 18 Pro is about to debut, and with a major shake-up to this year's lineup, it is set to become Apple's new default iPhone like never before.

There will be no base iPhone 18 this year, making the iPhone 18 Pro Apple's default new model.

For years, Apple has released multiple new iPhones each year, and that will undoubtedly continue for many years to come.

But at this week's Apple event, the iPhone lineup will undergo a major reshuffle.

Apple will not release the typical 'iPhone' and 'iPhone Pro' versions this time, and the base iPhone 18 will be entirely absent.

Multiple sources indicate that Apple will delay the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, meaning the autumn lineup will consist only of the following models:

The iPhone 18 Pro's launch has been pushed back from its usual schedule, effectively making it Apple's new default model.

Users seeking an affordable phone can still opt for the iPhone 17 released last year, or the iPhone 17e and iPhone Air. However, no matter how Apple or its carrier partners promote this autumn and holiday season, there will be no 'iPhone 18' to serve as the flagship new device. That role will be taken over by the iPhone 18 Pro.

The iPhone Ultra is priced too high, and its market positioning may be quite niche in comparison.

So for the average person looking to buy a 'new iPhone', Apple will essentially offer only two choices: the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

This approach is an interesting experiment, and it could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model of the new generation. But coupled with the expected price hike, there are certain risks involved. With no iPhone 18 on the market to upgrade to, potential buyers may hold on to their existing iPhones for longer.

Whatever the outcome, we will soon find out whether Apple's new strategy is a success.

What do you think of Apple's iPhone lineup changes this year? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
